title: Untargeted metabolomics of sera from mouse with lung cancer induced cachexia
description: Cancer cachexia is a multifactorial syndrome featured by a rapid reduction of body weight and accounts for 20-40% of cancer-related death. However, its underlying mechanism is poorly understood. We performed untargeted metabolomics analysis of serum samples from 4 health and 4 cachectic mouse to investigate the cachexia related metabolic change. In the cachexia group,1x106 LLC cells in 100 ul PBS was subcutaneously injected to the right flank of mice. Serum samples were collected 24 days after cancer cells injection. Untargeted LC-MS profiling of polar metabolites was performed on a UPLC (Waters Corp, ACQUITY I-Class) coupled with tandem ESI-QTOF mass spectrometry (Waters Corp, Synapt G2-Si). The acquired MS data pretreatment were performed using the Progenesis QI software. The online HMDB database was used to align the molecular mass data (m/z) and label the possible metabolite of each peak. This work identified differential metabolites in sera form cachectic mouse.

Tissue samples were collected 24 days after cancer cells injection.The phosphopeptides were analyzed by Easy-NLC 1200 liquid chromatography system (Thermo Fisher Scientific, USA) coupled to Orbitrap Fusion Lumos LC-MS/MS system (Thermo Fisher Scientific, USA). title: lncRNA IL6-AS1 promotes inflammatory effects in lung macrophages via exosomes through the S100A9/TLR4 pathway in COPD progression
description: This study investigates the role of IL6-AS1, a highly expressed long non-coding RNA (lncRNA), in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). An adeno-associated virus (AAV) was used to induce the expression of IL6-AS1 in mice, and they were exposed to cigarette smoke to establish a COPD model. Our findings indicate that the upregulation of IL6-AS1 in fibroblasts enhances the interaction between the S100A9 protein and the AGER and TLR4 receptors on lung macrophages, thereby exacerbating inflammatory responses. These findings suggest that IL6-AS1 may play a role in facilitating the crosstalk between fibroblasts and macrophages, leading to increased pulmonary inflammation. Mendelian randomization analysis further suggests a potential shared causal variant between IL6-AS1 and COPD. Taken together, this investigation provides valuable insights into the function of IL6-AS1 and its potential implications for the pathogenesis and therapeutic strategies in COPD.

title: Integrative plasma metabolomics predicts the onset and progression of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease

We show that unique plasma metabolic profiles successfully distinguish COPD patients from healthy controls and accurately separate emphysema and small-airway-dominant subtypes in validation cohorts. Crucially, a minimal 27-metabolite panel detects early COPD by capturing systemic metabolic shifts prior to actual lung function loss, while longitudinal subsets independently predict lung function decline, exacerbations, and dyspnea. Overall, plasma metabolomics yields robust, multi-purpose biomarkers, offering an accessible strategy for early screening and personalized clinical risk stratification.

title: Proteomic Profiling of Extracellular Vesicles Derived from P63+ Lung Progenitor Cells
description: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a progressive respiratory disorder characterized by inflammation of the airways, alveoli, and microvasculature, leading to emphysema and chronic bronchitis. As the third leading cause of death worldwide, current therapies remain largely palliative, with limited effect on disease progression or mortality. Regenerative strategies involving lung-resident stem/progenitor cells offer promising therapeutic potential. In this study, we investigated the role of P63+ lung progenitor cells in COPD repair. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from these cells, delivered via nebulization, promoted angiogenesis, epithelial regeneration, and improved lung function.

description: HNSCC arises from the mucosal epithelium of the oral cavity, pharynx, and larynx. ICI therapies, including PD-L1-targeting agents, have substantially improved HNSCC patients' survival. However, the mechanisms underlying ICI resistance remain incompletely understood. To clarify these mechanisms, we used single-cell RNA sequencing to analyze tumor samples from 5 Sintilimab-treated HNSCC patients. Our data identified all major cell types, revealed consistent expression patterns in non-malignant cells across all patients (both resistant and responsive), and showed that immune cell composition-particularly intratumoral T cell proportions-correlated with immunotherapeutic efficacy. Targeting TESC markedly enhances the engulfment of dying tumor cells by antigen-presenting cells, thereby promoting CD8+ T cell function and potentiating the therapeutic efficacy of anti-PD-1 antibodies.

title: lung adenocarcinoma metabolome
description: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) accounts for approximately 40% of non-small cell lung cancer. title: Transcriptomic sequencing of lung tissues from mice exposed to natural high-altitude environment and hypobaric chamber-simulated high-altitude environment
description: The number of people traveling or working for short-term stays at high altitudes has been increasing annually, and many of them develop high-altitude sickness.Further damage to lung and brain tissues may occur, which can be fatal in severe cases. At present, most studies on pulmonary diseases caused by high-altitude hypoxia use hypobaric chambers to simulate high-altitude environments. However, it remains unclear whether there are differences between hypobaric chamber exposure and natural high-altitude environment in terms of hypoxia-induced lung injury. This study used transcriptomic profiling to investigate similarities and differences in gene expression and signaling pathway alterations in mouse lung tissues between the natural high-altitude group and the hypobaric chamber group under equivalent hypoxic conditions, aiming to clarify the application value of hypobaric chamber models in research on high-altitude hypoxia-induced lung injury.

title: Targeting the Microglial Lipid-Lysosome Axis Overcomes Immunotherapy Resistance in Brain Metastases_metabolism
description: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionized cancer treatment, yet their efficacy against brain metastases (BrM) remains severely limited by a specialized, immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. In this study, we unveil a novel metabolic-immune crosstalk mechanism driving ICI resistance in BrM. Using single-cell RNA sequencing and high-resolution spatial transcriptomics, we identified a distinct subpopulation of SPP1+ TREM2+ lipid-associated microglia that prominently emerges under immunotherapy pressure. We demonstrate that these microglia undergo profound lipid accumulation and excessive lipophagy, ultimately culminating in lysosomal dysfunction and impaired antigen degradation.

title: RNA sequencing analysis of KPC-derived syngeneic orthotopic PDAC tissues treated with TROP2-targeting aptamer drug conjugate T17-M
description: This project contains transcriptomic profiles of KPC-derived syngeneic orthotopic PDAC tissues collected from in vivo therapeutic studies evaluating the antitumor effects and molecular responses induced by a TROP2-targeting aptamer-drug conjugate. Total RNA was extracted from tumor tissues, and mRNA sequencing libraries were generated and sequenced using the DNBSEQ-T7 platform with paired-end 150 bp reads. Sequencing reads were processed for quality control, adapter trimming, and removal of low-quality reads. Clean reads were aligned to the mouse reference genome, and gene expression levels were quantified and normalized as transcripts per kilobase million (TPM).
